facts.fact: The page states that CTV ads delivered non-skippable formats with high completion rates, averaging 94.5% per 15-second ad (figure linked to StackAdapt's connected TV stats page).
facts.quote: The non-skippable nature of CTV ads delivers high completion rates, [averaging 94.5%](https://www.stackadapt.com/resources/blog/connected-tv-stats) per 15-second ad.

facts.fact: The page cites an eMarketer forecast projecting that CTV ad spending will nearly double between 2026 and 2030, reaching $60.89 billion USD.
facts.quote: between 2026 and 2030, CTV ad spending is projected to nearly double, reaching [$60.89 billion USD]

facts.fact: The page states that CTV targeting is typically at the household level using identifiers such as IP addresses or household IDs that may be shared across multiple people.
facts.quote: Data-driven audience targeting, typically at the household level using identifiers such as IP addresses or household IDs that may be shared across multiple people.

facts.fact: The page states that OLV targeting is typically at the individual or device level using identifiers such as cookies, mobile advertising IDs, and logged-in user IDs.
facts.quote: often at the individual or device level using identifiers such as cookies, mobile advertising IDs, and logged-in user IDs.

facts.fact: The page states that OLV measurement supports both click-through and view-through measurement, along with engagement data such as quartile completion, pause, mute, viewability, and on-site behavior.
facts.quote: Supports both click-through and view-through measurement, along with more detailed engagement data such as quartile completion, pause, mute, viewability, and on-site behavior.

facts.fact: The page states that CTV measurement is primarily impression- and completion-based, with view-through measurement used to connect exposure to downstream actions.
facts.quote: Primarily impression- and completion-based, with view-through measurement used to connect ad exposure to downstream actions.

facts.fact: The page lists Roku, Hulu, Tubi, and Peacock as examples of streaming platforms through which CTV advertising delivers targeted video ads.
facts.quote: delivers targeted video ads across streaming platforms and services, such as Roku, Hulu, Tubi, and Peacock

facts.fact: The page states that marketers frequently access premium CTV inventory through private marketplaces (PMPs), programmatic guaranteed deals, or publisher-specific packages such as tentpole or live event programming.
facts.quote: Marketers frequently access premium CTV inventory through private marketplaces (PMPs), [programmatic guaranteed deals]

facts.fact: StackAdapt's page cites eMarketer in saying programmatic video ad spending is reaching $151.14 billion USD in 2026.
facts.quote: programmatic video ad spending is on the rise, reaching [$151.14 billion USD in 2026]

facts.fact: The page cites eMarketer in stating that programmatic video ad spending is increasing 23% year-over-year.
StackAdapt states that CTV spots often stick to 15- and 30-second lengths, matching traditional linear TV commercial structures.
facts.quote: CTV spots often stick to 15- and 30-second lengths, matching traditional linear TV commercial structures.

facts.fact: StackAdapt states that OLV versioning can include six-second bumpers and 15-second pre-rolls, among other formats.
facts.quote: Versioning can include six-second bumpers, 15-second pre-rolls, horizontal 16:9 spots, vertical 9:16 video, and 1:1 square formats

facts.fact: StackAdapt recommends OLV creative use front-loaded hooks where the entire message is revealed in the first three seconds.
facts.quote: front-loaded hooks where the entire message is revealed in the first three seconds

facts.fact: StackAdapt's guidance says a broadcast-quality, 15- to 30-second spot anchors a CTV campaign, while feed-based environments require edits, captions, and fast-paced hooks.
facts.quote: A broadcast-quality, 15- to 30-second spot anchors a CTV campaign, but video ads require edits, captions, and fast-paced hooks to succeed in feed-based environments.

facts.fact: StackAdapt defines CTV advertising as ads shown during programming delivered through streaming services viewed on smart TVs, streaming sticks, laptops, and gaming consoles.
facts.quote: CTV advertising specifically refers to ads shown during programming delivered through streaming services viewed on smart TVs, streaming sticks, laptops, and gaming consoles.

facts.fact: Programmatic advertising helps advertisers plan, buy, target, measure, and optimize video and TV campaigns across fragmented viewing environments from one platform.
facts.quote: Programmatic advertising helps advertisers plan, buy, target, measure, and optimize video and TV campaigns across fragmented viewing environments—all from one platform.
